items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: I don't know exactly when or how often Pee-wee played in Chicago, but you can't discuss Chicago style without discussing Pee-wee's playing

ctx.x: My feeling is along the same lines, yes.

Both you and I, I believe, feel that the Chicago School, as far as clarinet was concerned, was based on the inventions or the conceptions or the styles of the school. The styles of Teschmacher and Pee-wee-Pee-wee, not distinctly a Chicagoan, historically speaking, but yet so compatible with the Chicago style. Well, first of all, is that assumption correct, that they might have founded the elements of the Chicago style, as far as clarinet?

It's my assumption, yes. The actual historical business is vague to me. I don't know exactly when or how often Pee-wee played in Chicago, but you can't discuss Chicago style without discussing Pee-wee's playing, I don't think.
